title: Bilirubin–albumin interactions failed to improve frozen handgrip prediction beyond ALBI and additive markers in reused NHANES cohorts
abstract: We tested whether a25-term bilirubin-by-albumin spline surface adds concurrent combined-handgrip information beyond ALBI, separate marker splines, demographics, body size and creatinine. Training used NHANES2011–2012 (n=4007); frozen evaluation used separately recruited2013–2014 participants (n=4530). Examination-weighted target MSE increased from 135.234 to 157.230 kg². The registered improvement criterion failed. Joint source-refit/target PSU bootstrap uncertainty was highly dispersed: delta95% interval [5.401,20186.351] kg². Stronger scale-floor and liver-test restriction sensitivities also failed to improve MSE. This is an exploratory negative model-transfer audit, not a physiological null, causal inference or independent-program confirmation.
